explanation: The FTC's historical complaint describes the brand, fees, control and support behind a license label. These are allegations; official reports record settlement, while signed final-order remedy terms remain unreviewed.
The January 2024 entity default judgment addresses income, payback and support representations. It is a historical default judgment, not a contested trial or proof that ordered money was collected.

The 1996 commercial-cleaning consent decree connects earnings claims and records. It used the earlier disclosure framework, resolved disputed issues without admission, and does not replace today's Item 19 rules.

The identified 2025 janitorial consent judgment records admissions concerning classification, overtime and payroll records. Its terms and admissions belong to that case; they are not an automatic outcome for another employer.

The FTC’s 2026 complaint alleges unsupported semi-absentee claims, incomparable earnings cohorts and omitted external sales-management personnel. The reviewed settlement papers are proposed filings with blank judicial signature fields; no entered judgment or collected money is verified.
